title: Paul Asadoorian
name: Paul Asadoorian
summary: Paul Asadoorian is a security practitioner, educator, author, and podcaster known for founding Security Weekly and for work on penetration testing, firmware security, vulnerability management, and community education.
whyThisMatters: Asadoorian helped build a durable public forum for security practitioners through Security Weekly. His combination of technical practice, books, conference presentations, and long-form interviews has connected research to a broad professional audience.
knownFor: Work in penetration testing and vulnerability management
Research and advocacy around firmware and supply-chain security

sections.overview:
Paul Asadoorian is a security practitioner and communicator who founded Security Weekly, a podcast network covering information security and hacking. He has held technical roles in universities, consulting, and security-product companies.

His technical interests include penetration testing, vulnerability management, embedded devices, firmware, and supply-chain security. In 2007 he co-authored WRT54G Ultimate Hacking, a book focused on embedded-device and wireless experimentation.

Security Weekly gave practitioners a recurring forum for news, technical discussion, and interviews. Its community value is rooted in sustained, accessible conversation rather than a single vulnerability or product.

timeline.event: Works at Tenable and builds material on vulnerability management.
Security Weekly is acquired by CyberRisk Alliance.
Focuses publicly on firmware and supply-chain security and continues security-community work.
